meta.title: Records heist · cover-up
meta.note: Real model run (claude-haiku-5-5, fast mode: one agent) through the budget gateway, with one recorded question answer. The incident is a scripted scenario.

items.text: Run all deterministic checks in parallel

finding.rationale: The collector holds the records-app export_bulk line for adm-tkim (patients_full, 19527091 bytes, seq 557, 13:08:51) that is absent from the host-local access.log, though local records bracket it on both sides. The only local rotation was at 09:07:04, so rotation does not explain the absence. Host-local log is writable, so this is a claim of absence from the local copy only.
verifier_notes: 1 cited collector record(s) are absent from the local log after the host's retention boundary, bracketed by later local records

finding.rationale: Shell history records records-dump of patients_full written to /srv/records/tmp/cache-0a91.bin by adm-tkim at 13:08:50; the file stat shows 19527091 bytes owned by adm-tkim at 13:08:53, matching the export size.
verifier_notes: an object of matching size was written on this host shortly before a non-approved bulk transfer

finding.rationale: Tap flow shows 19530951 bytes sent from records (10.20.0.10) to 10.20.9.29:8080 at 13:11:25-13:11:38. Shell history records curl upload of /srv/records/tmp/cache-0a91.bin to that address. 10.20.9.29 is not an approved bulk destination and no change record covers it. The sending session was records#461, a remote adm-tkim session from VPN 10.20.0.250.
verifier_notes: bulk transfer to a destination not on the approved list, cited via the flow record

finding.rationale: 8.4 MB immunization_registry transfer to 10.20.9.35:8443 is named in approved change record CHG-8764 (quarterly state registry submission, window 08:27:59-09:27:59, requested by adm-tkim). It was a single export to that destination within the window.
verifier_notes: a deterministic check supports this observation; it is not an incident allegation

finding.rationale: The 19.5 MB patients_full export at 11:59 was started by the svc-backup scheduled job (backup-incremental) and sent to 10.20.0.45, the approved backup/archive NAS. This is a scheduled, policy-consistent transfer.
verifier_notes: references resolve; no allegation is made

limits: Remote session; badge records do not cover it
Shared console credentials have been found written down before
Host-local log and shell history are writable on the host; the collector copy is the independent witness for the export line
attribution.statement: Account adm-tkim (IT admin) was used for the unapproved patients_full export (exp-3, 13:08:51), its staging at /srv/records/tmp/cache-0a91.bin, the upload to 10.20.9.29:8080, and the removal of the export line from the host-local records access.log. The session was records#461, remote from VPN gateway 10.20.0.250. The human operator is not established: the account identifies a credential, and the remote session has no badge coverage.

report.summary: Bundle bndl-9023e573787c3b85 (Northside Clinic). Three records-server exports were reviewed. (1) 08:48 immunization_registry export by adm-tkim sent to 10.20.9.35:8443 is covered by approved change record CHG-8764: policy-consistent. (2) 11:59 patients_full export by svc-backup scheduled job sent to approved NAS 10.20.0.45: policy-consistent. (3) 13:08 patients_full export by adm-tkim has no covering change record. The shell history shows records-dump to /srv/records/tmp/cache-0a91.bin (19.5 MB, staged), and at 13:11 a curl upload of that file to 10.20.9.29:8080, which is not an approved destination (19.5 MB on the tap). The sending session was records#461, a remote adm-tkim session from VPN 10.20.0.250. Also, the collector holds the 13:08:51 export_bulk line for adm-tkim that is absent from the host-local records access.log, though bracketed by local records; the only rotation was at 09:07, so the absence is unexplained. Forwarding, file timestamps, cross-host sessions and shell-history gaps were clean. Sensor check not applicable. Attribution: the account adm-tkim was used; the human operator is not established, since account use is not person identity and the session was remote.
open_questions: Who operated records#461 (remote VPN session from 10.20.0.250)? Needs VPN logs and interview; badge data cannot cover it.
Who controls 10.20.9.29:8080? It is not on the approved list; identify the destination.
Was the access.log line removal done by adm-tkim or another actor? Host-local writable; confirm via any other copy of the line.
Was the local absence of the export line caused by tampering or a logging fault? Only the collector copy shows it.

questions.question: Was the export from the records server approved, and where did the data go?
questions.answer: Two of three records-server exports were approved. The 08:48 immunization_registry export (adm-tkim) was covered by CHG-8764 and went to 10.20.9.35:8443. The 11:59 patients_full export (svc-backup scheduled job) went to approved NAS 10.20.0.45. The 13:08:51 patients_full export by adm-tkim has no covering change record. Its 19.5 MB was staged at /srv/records/tmp/cache-0a91.bin and sent to 10.20.9.29:8080, which is not an approved destination. The sending session was records#461, a remote adm-tkim session from VPN 10.20.0.250. The account was used; the human operator is not established.

limitations: Account adm-tkim identifies a credential, not a person; the remote operator is not established and badge data does not cover VPN sessions.
The local access.log and shell history are host-writable; the absent line is shown only by the collector copy.
Flow records show byte volume, not content; the 10.20.9.29 destination's owner is unknown.
Account activity identifies a credential, not the person using it. This evidence does not establish who that was, and does not clear anyone.
follow_up_evidence: VPN gateway logs for the 10.20.0.250 session that became records#461, to identify the source endpoint.
Ownership and records for 10.20.9.29:8080, and any change request covering it.
An independent copy of the access.log line or the destination's receipt log.
